Post-Campaign Recap · Illustrative Template

What we learned from the Q2 launch, in numbers we can defend.

Thirty days, four channels, one product launch. This page is a working recap — every chart runs off small JSON blocks you can see and edit directly in this file, and every headline metric carries an explicit source note. The figures below are illustrative placeholders chosen to make the structure usable; replace them with your own data before circulating.

Reporting window: 2026-05-01 → 2026-05-30 (30 days) · Campaign: Q2 product launch · Owner: Growth · Currency: USD · Last updated: 2026-07-13

The headline in one paragraph

The launch cleared its top-of-funnel targets but under-delivered on bottom-funnel efficiency. Paid social carried reach, search closed the click, influencer content did most of the brand-lift work, and email punched well above its weight on retention. The single biggest issue was a thin mid-funnel — site visits converted to leads at almost half the rate we planned for, which is what pulled blended CAC above the target ceiling.

Bottom line. We hit reach and awareness, missed efficiency, and learned a clear rule for the next launch: protect mid-funnel conversion rate at least as hard as top-of-funnel volume.

Headline KPIs vs. plan

Six numbers summarize the campaign. The plan column is what was signed off in the Q2 brief; the actual column is the agreed measurement source shown beneath the chart.

Total spend $148.2k vs. plan $150.0k · 98.8%
Impressions 12.4M vs. plan 11.0M · 113%
Site sessions 186k vs. plan 175k · 106%
Qualified leads 3,210 vs. plan 4,200 · 76.4%
Customers 412 vs. plan 480 · 85.8%
Blended CAC $359 vs. plan $313 · 14.7% over

Where actuals diverged from plan

Reach and awareness metrics cleared plan; conversion metrics did not. The widest gap is on qualified leads, which is the same gap the funnel chart below explains in stage form.

Where the money and the credit went

Spend was spread roughly evenly across four channels. Attribution tells a different story: paid search did most of the closing work even though it carried only a quarter of the spend, while influencer content produced shareable proof that the rest of the campaign redistributed onto. This is the chart to look at when the CFO asks why blended CAC is what it is.

Where the funnel thinned

Five stages, every one of them instrumented. The visible bottleneck is between sessions and qualified leads: every other stage ratio sits within plan, that one runs at 1.7% actual against a 2.4% plan target. The next section breaks the timing down by day so you can see where the loss occurred.

Shape of the thirty days

Two things are visible in the daily series: a strong opening week driven by influencer drops on days 2–4 and 8–10, and a flatlining second half. Sessions held shape, but lead capture did not. That gap is the launch's central data puzzle and is consistent across every channel except paid search.

What we learned, what we will change

  • Top-of-funnel efficiency is healthy. Impressions and CPM landed inside plan; we do not need to relearn reach.
  • Mid-funnel is the bottleneck. Sessions-to-leads under-delivered by 28% (1.73% vs 2.40% plan). Root cause is in qualitative review of landing-page analytics, not in media buying.
  • Paid search is the most efficient channel per dollar of attributed revenue. Influencer content is the most efficient channel for new-audience introduction. The next brief should not pit them against each other.
  • Email is small but does retention. 11.7% of spend, 13.5% of attributed revenue, and essentially all of the post-purchase retention. Keep it funded regardless of next-quarter mix.
  • Do not run the same brief twice. The flatlined second half was caused by creative fatigue plus a thin offer stack. Plan a creative refresh at day 14 in the next cycle.

Notes on method

Attribution. Revenue share is allocated using a last-non-direct touch model with a 30-day lookback. The numbers will shift under a different model (first-touch, linear, data-driven); the directional finding does not.
Currency and rounding. All values are USD. CAC and ratios are rounded to two significant figures for the headline strip and to one decimal in the funnel chart.
What's missing. Brand-lift study and post-purchase NPS by channel are not yet in this file. The team expects them by 2026-07-20; the recap will be amended, not republished, once they land.
